correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the verified real-valued constant-2 weak endpoint. The angular projection lemma is an exact calculation from the two-by-two Gram matrix of the real and imaginary parts of a complex vector. Integrating the real weak estimates over all phase rotations and using the exact scalar rotation integral yields 2/(c arccos c). The optimizer lies in the lemma's admissible range and is characterized exactly by theta*tan(theta)=1. No dimension-dependent coordinate reduction or unproved complex obstacle theory is used.

value.rationale: The source's real-only formulation leaves a natural endpoint gap because complex scalars are standard in Fourier and spectral harmonic analysis. Naive real/imaginary splitting gives a universal constant 4; the rotation geometry lowers this to 3.56445 while preserving full dimension and drift independence. The argument isolates a reusable Hilbert-target mechanism rather than merely restating the real theorem.
